title: Social VR spaces to hang out in
summary: Virtual worlds where people meet as avatars to chat, attend events, and spend time together.
keywords: virtual reality, metaverse, avatars, virtual events, VR social, headsets, virtual worlds
whyTempting: Being in a room with someone in VR feels genuinely different from a video call, and demos are memorable. Every new headset launch makes it feel like the audience is about to arrive.
whyItFails:
Only a small share of people own a headset, and fewer still wear it regularly. A social space needs a crowd to feel alive, so a small install base produces empty worlds, which then drive away the people who did show up.

Open spaces with strangers also attract harassment, which is more intense in VR than on a flat screen and expensive to moderate.
whatWouldChange:
A new attempt needs to work well for people without a headset (on phones or desktops) so it isn't waiting on hardware sales, or it needs a reason for a specific group to show up together at set times, such as classes, teams or events.

It also needs moderation and personal safety tools designed in from the start.

attempts.outcome: Acquired by Microsoft, then shut down

attempts.notes: A VR world platform from the makers of Second Life.
Meet friends as avatars in VR.

reasons.detail: Too few people own and regularly use a headset.
Empty worlds feel dead, so early visitors don't come back.
Harassment in shared spaces is intense and costly to manage.
Each wave of hardware arrived slower than the platforms needed.
